title: `length`, `reverse`, `trim`, `ascii`, `repeat`, `levenshtein`: code points, spaces only
verdict: code points throughout; `trim` strips U+0020 only; native
description: `length` and `char_length` count code points (`length('😀a')` is 2, a combining accent counts on its own), `octet_length` UTF-8 bytes. `reverse` reverses code points, so a combining accent moves to the other side of its letter. `trim`, `btrim`, `ltrim`, `rtrim` strip the space U+0020 only, never tabs or newlines; `trim(BOTH 'x' FROM s)` strips the given characters. `ascii('é')` is 233, the code point; `ascii('')` 0. `repeat('ab', -1)` is empty. `levenshtein` counts code points (`levenshtein('héllo', 'hello')` is 1).
Strings order and compare by UTF-8 bytes, which is code point order (`UTF8String.binaryCompare`), under the default `UTF8_BINARY` collation.
reference: `character_length` counts code points; `reverse` reverses them; `btrim(s)` trims spaces only; strings order by code point. Spark is native.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `ascii('§')`, `ascii('÷')`, `ascii('×10')` are 167, 247, 215: the code point, not the first UTF-8 byte

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
